subject: Recap: Integration primer — SDK changes & function-calling pilot
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Goldstein <ari@keystonehealth.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@keystonehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Integration primer — SDK changes & function-calling pilot

Thanks again for a productive conversation today — appreciate the time, Ari and Maya. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up a pilot.

Pain points you shared
- Triage agents are overwhelmed by false positives in the clinical intake stream; manual review ~45% of tickets.
- Current latency from triage → suggestion is inconsistent; multi-step enrichment adds 300-450ms per request.
- Security: PHI must remain in-region and logs must be retained for 7 years to satisfy audit.

Goals we heard
- Reduce manual review by ~30% within the pilot scope (triage NL classifier + embedding-based rerank).
- Keep 95th-percentile inference latency < 200ms for single-turn suggestions.
- End-to-end auditability: request-level tracing and per-token cost breakdowns.

What we demonstrated / fit notes
- Redwood hosted runtime supports streaming responses + function-calling to let you run lightweight enrichment (lookup patient history) server-side, minimizing client round trips.
- Embeddings + local reranker model fit your retrieval-heavy flows; we recommended 8k-context model for summaries.
- SDK changes needed: client will call new streaming SDK hook (on_chunk) and a function-calling shim (invoke_tool) to coordinate lookups and structured outputs.

Proposed pilot scope (4 weeks)
1) Week 0–1: Set up sandbox project in your VPC (Private) with region restriction (us-west-2).
2) Week 1–2: Integrate streaming SDK hooks and function-calling shim in a small triage microservice (2 endpoints).
3) Week 2–3: Run 50k synthetic requests + live shadowing; enable KV prefix caching to accelerate repeated tokens.
4) Week 3–4: Evaluate quality (false-positive reduction) and latency SLOs; decision gate for expansion.

Immediate asks (action owners)
- Ari / Maya: confirm that Keystone can provide a sample of anonymized intake events (S3 link) by Friday, 12/11.
- Marissa / Ben: produce a minimal SDK patch and a short integration guide (target: 12/15).
- Logan: prepare a scoped quote for Dedicated vs Private options and an initial runbook for audit traces.

Attachments: I attached a rough scope spreadsheet (keystone_mvp_scope.xlsx) and a minimal patch showing the streaming hook we discussed (redwood_sdk_patch.diff).

If that matches your expectations, I’ll schedule a short kickoff with engineering on Monday.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ari Goldstein <ari@keystonehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@keystonehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Integration primer — SDK changes & function-calling pilot

Thanks, Logan — solid write-up. A couple clarifying items: 

- Data residency: yes, we need the sandbox and any logs stored in us-west-2 only. Can you confirm the Private deployment package will keep all traces in-region?
- Latency: 95p < 200ms is aggressive but sounds achievable if we avoid a client-side enrichment hop. In your pilot plan, can the function-calling shim run as a co-located microservice in our VPC?
- Security artifacts: we’ll need SOC2 documentation and an initial runbook for how audit logs are exported/retained for our compliance team.

We can share a small sanitized S3 dataset by 12/11. Also looping in our infra lead to coordinate VPC peering if needed.

Ari
Director, Digital Ops
Keystone Health

Marissa here — quick internal notes on effort estimation and risks.
- SDK work: the streaming hook + function shim is about 3–4 dev days including test harness; need a small change to the client serializer to emit structured JSON outputs (so their downstream SLAed systems can parse suggestions).
- Infra: setting up Private sandbox + VPC peering estimate 2–3 infra days (security reviews may add slack).
- Risk: embeddings/rerank accuracy will depend on the retrieval unitization; suggest we include a small eval set in Week 2 to tune the reranker.

Actionable: I’ll draft the integration guide and a minimal example repo by 12/15. Ben — can you scope the infra tasks and flag any blockers for SOC2 evidence?

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Great — thanks for confirming, Ari. Quick updates and next steps: 

1) Private in-region: confirmed. We’ll provision a Private sandbox in us-west-2; all logs and KV caches stay in-region. I’ve added the SOC2 evidence packet to the Drive folder (link below).
2) Function-calling shim: yes — we recommend deploying the shim as a co-located microservice inside your VPC to meet the latency target; it’s included in the scope worksheet.
3) Timeline: Kickoff Monday 12/14 (30 min) — engineering owners only. Pilot start target: 12/16.

Please reply with a one-line approval to proceed and I’ll send calendar invites and a short pre-kickoff checklist.
